findings.title: Existing SQL expression tests will fail against the new stub DB
findings.body:
The new stub `RunCommands` and `QueryFramesInto` always return "not implemented". As a result `sql.TablesList` and `expr.NewSQLCommand` now always return an error.

Existing tests still assume they succeed and were not updated or skipped in this PR:
- `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go` (e.g. `TestParse`, which expects `TablesList("select * from foo")` to return `foo`).
- `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go` (`TestNewCommand`, which expects `NewSQLCommand("a", "select a from foo, bar")` to succeed).

These tests will fail CI. They should be skipped or rewritten to assert the new disabled behaviour.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has inverted naming and ignores the feature flag
findings.body:
`enableSqlExpressions` sets `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, so `enabled` is true when the flag is OFF. Both branches then return false, so the toggle is read but has no effect.

This is misleading. A future maintainer who edits one branch to "re-enable" the feature could easily get the polarity wrong and turn SQL expressions on when the flag is off, re-opening the RCE/LFI.

It also adds a needless dereference of `h.features` (a nil-features reader now panics on the SQL path).

User-facing problems:
- The `sqlExpressions` toggle is still registered and documented as enabling the feature, but it is now a silent no-op.
- The returned error says "sqlExpressions is not implemented" rather than that the feature is disabled.

Replace the function with an unconditional, clearly commented disable and a clear error message. Also update or deprecate the toggle docs.

findings.title: Legacy SQL expression path is not explicitly gated; relies only on the stub
findings.body:
The explicit disable check was added only in `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery`. The legacy graph-building path (`buildCMDNode` -> `UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand`) has no equivalent gate. It is blocked today only because the stub `sql.TablesList` happens to fail.

On that path users get a generic "error reading SQL command" BadRequest instead of a clear "disabled" error. The security fix also depends on the stub never being replaced with a real engine.

Add the same explicit rejection in `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` so both entry points are covered consistently.

findings.title: No regression test for the security disable
findings.body:
This PR is the in-repo version of the CVE-2024-9264 fix, but it adds no test asserting that a `type: sql` expression is rejected. That should be checked both with the `sqlExpressions` toggle on and off, and through both the `ReadQuery` and `UnmarshalSQLCommand` paths.

Without such a test, a future change could silently re-enable SQL expressions and nothing would catch it.

findings.title: Every SQL expression attempt now logs at Error level
findings.body:
With the stub DB, `RunCommands` always fails. So every SQL expression that reaches `TablesList` (e.g. via the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path) logs `logger.Error("error serializing sql", ...)`, which includes the full user-supplied SQL. `NewSQLCommand` then logs an additional Warn.

This is expected, permanent behaviour for a disabled feature, not an error condition. It creates log noise and records arbitrary user query text at error level.

Short-circuit before calling the stub, or lower the log level.
